title: Carnegie Hall double, Dinah Washington and Ray Charles as concert artist
summary: Ray Charles accepts a thousand dollars for both dates, Thomas adds Dinah Washington, and Thursday at Connors Beach proves his concert appeal.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: [END OF TAPE 4, SIDE A]

And he took the double date for the second... He didn't ask for no more... I was giving him a thousand dollars a date. He didn't ask for another penny to double from Newark to Carnegie Hall. But I always will believe...
A thousand dollars for both dates?
Yes.
That wasn't fair.

No! But he okayed it. I didn't want to say nothin' more about it, because he okayed it, and...he said "Yes." I told them, "Oh yes," and they went and booked it. And he broke it up. That's the first time he played Carnegie Hall. But I found out those Rock-and-Roll musicians, it's an honor for them to play Carnegie Hall.
Thomas - 178
Well, it should be an honor for anyone.
But...

Don't you think that's right, Foots? An agent... If you're booking like two places a night, and three ...(?)..., even if he okayed it, he didn't know... He's not aware of what the booking is. You might even say, 'Well, okay, here's a couple of hundred dollars extra for you?'

But he still got a thousand dollars for it. But the thing is that the promoter had the three days. He didn't do too good in Boston. He broke even in Boston. And I got the idea of putting a singer, Dinah Washington... I knew they were friends, see, and Dinah Washington really made sense, because she's a girl singer, which didn't have nothin' to do with him being a piano player and a singer -- and he liked Dinah anyway. And Dinah's records were kind of big then. So I got them together. And it worked out all right, because the guy would have lost money in Richmond, because Richmond was a flop. So by doing the double... But the one good that came out of it, it made him a concert artist.
It made him a what?
A concert artist. He started playing concerts after that. One guy that I was involved with
Thomas - 179
booking concerts...
And then somebody else got a chance to book him because he came in with the right money.

Yeah, right. And this guy got an idea. And he put Ray Charles... He was afraid of him doing it on his own. So he put Ray Charles with two or three other people, and he booked some concerts throughout different areas. And they gave me the first date. I took a Thursday down in Connors(?) Beach. See, I knew my territory. Connors(?) Beach is down at Annapolis; it's right across from Annapolis. And I knew what kind of business he could do in Connors(?) Beach, because down there a Thursday night for Ray Charles was just as good as a Friday night, and he had them other artists. It was a big show, like...
Why is it just as good?
Because they ain't got but one more day to work, and if they can make it over that night, then you've just got Friday, and they're off Saturday and Sunday -- so they'll go on Thursday night.
And my date turned out to be the biggest date on the tour. But we found out from that, that Ray Charles was a concert artist. But the first dates I booked on him proved that he was a concert artist.
